title: infrastructure-weekly-update-2026-04-06
content:
Infrastructure Weekly Update — 2026-04-06

Summary:
- This week focused on managing near-term GPU capacity for Q2 spike, region balancing, and finishing the autoscaler tuning for batch inference workloads.
- No sev1 incidents; one recurring degradation in us-east-1 pre-warm pool observed and mitigated via temporary quota bump.

GPU fleet status:
- Total rentable GPUs (prod pools): 1,840 (A100 80GB and mixed 80/40 pools). Utilization: 68% average across peaks (08:00–20:00).
- Pre-warm pools (for low-latency workloads): 220 GPUs; target buffer is 15% of steady-state for hosted API. Current buffer ~12% — short by ~40 GPUs for projected growth next week.
- Recent hardware onboarding: 160x A100-80GB arrived at us-west-2 rack 12; integration complete. Initial perf tests show ~3% lower throughput vs baseline due to PCIe config (tracking in linked ticket).
- H100 pilot: 8 H100 nodes deployed in eu-west-1 for eval jobs. Early results show 25–40% lower p99 latency on long-context generation but require kernel tuning for fp16 paths.

Regions & capacity planning:
- us-east-1: steady-state load up 14% week-over-week. Autoscaler target set to conservative for now due to ongoing pre-warm flapping (see Incidents). Planned scale +80 GPUs on 2026-04-09 to maintain 99.9% latency SLO during peak.
- us-west-2: newly integrated capacity available; routing policy will shift some Dedicated traffic to us-west-2 next Tues (2026-04-07) to validate routing and egress patterns.
- eu-west-1: H100 pilot + existing A100 pools. Recommend enabling H100-backed routes for select test customers next week.
- ap-southeast-1: no new capacity. Monitoring shows slow but steady adoption — we expect to add a small burst-capacity allocation mid-May if usage continues.

Autoscaler & scheduling work:
- Canary of new continuous-batching-friendly autoscaler ran in prod for batch-inference route B (PR #210). Results: 7% cost reduction for heavy long-context jobs, slight increase in queueing time for sub-50ms requests.
- Action: tuning scheduled to reduce batching window for low-latency routes while keeping batching for high-throughput routes. Owners: Evan (autoscaler) + Priya (routing policies).

Incidents / Reliability:
- Incident (non-sev): pre-warm pool in us-east-1 degraded intermittently 2026-04-03 03:20–04:10 UTC due to node-level kernel panic after a driver update. Mitigation: roll back driver on affected hosts and replace 12 pre-warm nodes. Root cause: driver/firmware mismatch on a small subset of vendor images. Follow-up: vendor firmware audit scheduled (JIRA-ENGINFRA-482).
- No customer-facing impact thanks to cross-region fallback policies but internal autoscaler metrics showed a spike in cold-starts (~18 extra cold starts during window).

Operational metrics (last 7 days):
- Avg token throughput (hosted): 1.1B tokens/day
- Peak p95 latency (text-gen): 410ms
- Mean GPU utilization (prod pools): 68%
- Pre-warm hit-rate (hosted low-latency routes): 86% (target 90%)

Standups / highlights this week:
- Daily infra standups continuing at 09:30 PT; rotating focus on regions. Attendance average: 12 engineers.
- Cross-team sync with Product and SRE on rollout plan for Dedicated routing changes (completed Thurs).
- Completed infra-config PR to add us-west-2 routing weights (github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/pull/210).

Action items / next week:
- Add 40 GPUs to pre-warm pools in us-east-1 by 2026-04-09 (owner: Evan).
- Complete H100 kernel tuning and document perf deltas (owner: Luca). Target: 2026-04-14.
- Finish autoscaler tuning for low-latency routes — reduce batching window from 250ms -> 100ms for route A (owner: Priya).
- Vendor firmware audit kickoff and remediation plan (owner: Samira).
- Create postmortem draft for 2026-04-03 pre-warm degradation (owner: Samira, due 2026-04-08).

Risks & blockers:
- Hardware supply: delivery ETA for additional A100 nodes slipped from late April to early May for one vendor; contingency stocks may be required. Finance and procurement looped in.
- Firmware/driver heterogeneity across racks increasing failure surface; audit needed to avoid repeat.

Notes / links:
- Capacity plan (Q2): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFRA/GPU+Capacity+Plan
- Related Jira: JIRA-ENGINFRA-482 (pre-warm driver rollback)
- infra-config PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/pull/210

Meeting invites / reminders:
- Q2 capacity review w/ Finance & Product: 2026-04-13 16:00 PT
- H100 pilot review: 2026-04-15 10:00 PT

Appendix (quick numbers):
- GPUs by region (prod pools): us-east-1: 820, us-west-2: 460, eu-west-1: 360, ap-southeast-1: 200
- Expected additional GPUs (incoming): 160 A100 (us-west-2) already integrated; next shipment ~200 A100 expected early May (vendor TBC).

Notes to self: rough checklist for next week:
- confirm us-east-1 pre-warm increase + monitor for cold starts
- validate routing weight changes after traffic shift to us-west-2
- get procurement confirmation on delayed shipment
- follow up on H100 perf note and whether to expand to more routes

End of update.
